denoiser.text:
U-Net denoiser
The network applied at every step: a 3-stage convolutional U-net (down → mid → up with skip connections) that takes the latent z_t (+ timestep + text conditioning) and predicts the noise. Each down stage halves the spatial resolution (the latent is 4× downscaled at the bottleneck) and each up stage doubles it back; the timestep modulates every ResNet, and text conditioning (dim 2048) enters the cross-attention stages. latent.text:
Latent state (z_t)
The working latent — a single slot the loop reads and rewrites each step. It is seeded once from the initial noise (z_T), overwritten every step by the scheduler's output (z_{t-1}), and read by the denoiser as the current z_t. 'z_t' and 'z_{t-1}' are this same slot at consecutive steps, not separate tensors — the two arrows feeding it are two writers at different times, not a sum.
4 channels

noise.text:
Initial noise
z_T: random Gaussian latent, shape [4 channels], sampled in the VAE latent space. (Image-to-image instead starts from an encoded input image.) This is the latent the loop iteratively denoises.

prompt.text:
Text prompt
The conditioning prompt, encoded by 2 text encoders (CLIP (768-d), CLIP (1,280-d)). Their token features are concatenated along the feature axis (768 + 1,280 = 2,048-d) into the cross-attention conditioning.

sch_pred.text:
Predicted noise
The denoiser's predicted noise (ε̂) for this timestep, handed to the scheduler each step.

sch_scale.text:
σ_t · ε̂
Scales the predicted noise by this timestep's noise level σ_t.

sch_step.text:
Combine step
Combines the current latent z_t with the scaled prediction to take one denoising step toward z_{t-1} (the ⊕ glyph).

sch_zt.text:
Current latent z_t
The latent being denoised — the loop-carried value the scheduler updates into z_{t-1}.

scheduler.text:
Scheduler — Euler
Euler combines the denoiser's prediction with z_t to produce z_{t-1}, one step toward a clean latent. The loop repeats for N sampling steps (N chosen at inference, typically ~20-50 — it is not a config field).

text_concat_op.text:
Concatenate (feature axis)
The encoders' per-token features are joined along the feature (channel) axis — stacked side by side into wider tokens, with no projection, no mixing and no added parameters. Here 768 + 1,280 = 2,048. That combined tensor is the keys/values every cross-attention stage reads. It is the same operation (torch.cat over the feature axis) as the U-net's skip connections — which is why both use the ‖ connector, not ⊕.
→ 2,048-d K/V

timestep.text:
Timestep
The current step's noise level t (decreasing T -> 0). Embedded, then projected and added inside every ResNet block (and the mid block) — a U-net conditions on the noise level additively, not through AdaLN. SDXL also adds a micro-conditioning embedding — the pooled text vector together with the image size / crop / target-size ('time_ids') embeddings, projected from 2,816-d — to this timestep embedding (addition_embed_type = text_time).

unet_op_conv1.text:
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.

unet_op_conv2.text:
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.

unet_op_norm1.text:
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.

unet_op_norm2.text:
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.

unet_op_residual.text:
Residual add
Adds the block's raw input back onto the convolved output — (input_tensor + hidden_states) / output_scale_factor. The bypass goes around the entire cell: norm1, SiLU, conv1, timestep injection, norm2, SiLU, conv2. When in/out channels differ a 1×1 conv adjusts the shortcut (conv_shortcut).

unet_op_temb.text:
⊕ Timestep embedding
The linear-projected timestep embedding is added here (ResnetBlock2D: hidden_states = hidden_states + time_emb_proj(SiLU(temb))). This is the mechanism by which a UNet ResNet receives the current noise level — distinct from DiT/AdaLN, which gates normalization parameters. The projection adjusts the channel width to match the residual branch.

unet_text_cond.text:
Text conditioning
The encoded text prompt supplies the keys/values to EVERY cross-attention stage — the down, mid and up CrossAttn blocks all read the same 2048-d text states, the 2 text encoders' token features concatenated along the feature axis (768 + 1,280 = 2,048). The latent flows through the U vertically; this conditioning enters each cross-attention stage from the side. Click to see how the encoders combine. Declared by cross_attention_dim + the CrossAttn* block types.

Doubles spatial resolution (H × W → 2H × 2W) by nearest-neighbour interpolation, then a 3×3 conv to smooth interpolation artifacts. Runs once after the ResNet stack, stepping the latent toward image size.

Initial noise
z_T: random Gaussian latent, shape [4 channels], sampled in the VAE latent space. (Image-to-image instead starts from an encoded input image.) This is the latent the loop iteratively denoises.
Timestep
The current step's noise level t (decreasing T -> 0). Embedded, then projected and added inside every ResNet block (and the mid block) — a U-net conditions on the noise level additively, not through AdaLN. SDXL also adds a micro-conditioning embedding — the pooled text vector together with the image size / crop / target-size ('time_ids') embeddings, projected from 2,816-d — to this timestep embedding (addition_embed_type = text_time).
Text prompt
The conditioning prompt, encoded by 2 text encoders (CLIP (768-d), CLIP (1,280-d)). Their token features are concatenated along the feature axis (768 + 1,280 = 2,048-d) into the cross-attention conditioning.

Latent state (z_t)
The working latent — a single slot the loop reads and rewrites each step. It is seeded once from the initial noise (z_T), overwritten every step by the scheduler's output (z_{t-1}), and read by the denoiser as the current z_t. 'z_t' and 'z_{t-1}' are this same slot at consecutive steps, not separate tensors — the two arrows feeding it are two writers at different times, not a sum.

U-Net denoiser
The network applied at every step: a 3-stage convolutional U-net (down → mid → up with skip connections) that takes the latent z_t (+ timestep + text conditioning) and predicts the noise. Each down stage halves the spatial resolution (the latent is 4× downscaled at the bottleneck) and each up stage doubles it back; the timestep modulates every ResNet, and text conditioning (dim 2048) enters the cross-attention stages. Concatenate (feature axis)
The encoders' per-token features are joined along the feature (channel) axis — stacked side by side into wider tokens, with no projection, no mixing and no added parameters. Here 768 + 1,280 = 2,048. That combined tensor is the keys/values every cross-attention stage reads. It is the same operation (torch.cat over the feature axis) as the U-net's skip connections — which is why both use the ‖ connector, not ⊕.
→ 2,048-d K/V

Group normalization followed by a SiLU (swish) activation, applied before each convolution in the residual cell. Normalizes feature statistics so the conv sees a well-scaled signal.

Doubles spatial resolution (H × W → 2H × 2W) by nearest-neighbour interpolation, then a 3×3 conv to smooth interpolation artifacts. Runs once after the ResNet stack, stepping the latent toward image size.

Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.
⊕ Timestep embedding
The linear-projected timestep embedding is added here (ResnetBlock2D: hidden_states = hidden_states + time_emb_proj(SiLU(temb))). This is the mechanism by which a UNet ResNet receives the current noise level — distinct from DiT/AdaLN, which gates normalization parameters. The projection adjusts the channel width to match the residual branch.
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.
Residual add
Adds the block's raw input back onto the convolved output — (input_tensor + hidden_states) / output_scale_factor. The bypass goes around the entire cell: norm1, SiLU, conv1, timestep injection, norm2, SiLU, conv2. When in/out channels differ a 1×1 conv adjusts the shortcut (conv_shortcut).
